actual_hybrid_path.basis: H009 deployed/qualification evidence plus exact baseline file_auth launch and H010 canonical harness status; no new backend contact
actual_hybrid_path.description: CPU expert offload integrated with CUDA model execution; conditional layerwise GPU expert staging is configured. Zero resident GPU experts is not CPU-only.

evidence.fact: The exact Glm5Next branch requires NVIDIA CUDA and explicitly excludes CPU, ROCm and NPU. This source file SHA256 exactly matches native-source-pins.json, independently of our deployment wrapper.
Generic device auto-selection/--device cpu exists elsewhere (1202-1203, 4152-4156), but the exact model accepts only checkpoint-native FP8. Generic CPU support does not override its model gate.
Exact model requires its trtllm-named NSA dispatcher for prefill/decode and GPU-profile cache precision; alternative generic attention backends are rejected.

evidence.area: Actual SM120 path versus library imports
evidence.fact: SM120 takes model-local sparse MLA before the FlashInfer import; decode selects its CUDA Triton kernel. Do not claim the SM120 route requires the FlashInfer TRTLLM ABI merely from dispatcher naming. Constructor nevertheless unconditionally queries torch.cuda capability (385); non-HIP module imports sgl_kernel FlashAttention (73-74).
Prefill invokes FLA l2norm_fwd and chunk_kda through Glm5NextTritonKDAKernel; no CPU extend selection in this adapter.

CPU causal-convolution update is imported conditionally, but the backend still selects Glm5NextTritonKDAKernel. CPU gate/decode reference helpers also exist in glm5_next_kda_ops.py (206-207, 478-494); these are not a complete CPU serving path.

A CPU reference branch exists and dequantizes the flat FP8 cache to BF16 for indexing. The source identifies this as a tiny unit-test oracle; it does not establish complete CPU serving or production-sized memory behavior.

Exact hybrid pool requires MLA plus HybridReqToTokenPool and allocates on model_runner.device; source allocators take a device argument but that does not make the surrounding serving backend CPU supported.

GLM constructs ParallelLMHead/logits processor; embedding construction is at730-734. Model loader initializes parameters under target_device (loader.py667-678). Official config excludes lm_head and model.embed_tokens from FP8. They are not an intrinsic CPU blocker in isolation, but there is no model-wide CPU flag override.

The general block-FP8 linear CPU branch requires AMX; apply dispatches fp8_scaled_mm_cpu at725-735. This is distinct from the KT AVX-512 expert kernel and is not evidence that all GLM non-expert layers can execute on the existing host. No fresh CPU ISA probe was authorized/performed.

evidence.area: CPU expert integration still requires CUDA
evidence.fact: Both ordinary expert submit and result synchronization obtain torch.cuda.current_stream even when resident GPU expert count is zero.

Positive kt_gpu_prefill_token_threshold enables layerwise GPU expert prefill and normalizes resident GPU expert count to zero. This describes configured conditional behavior; H010 Worker2 did not measure whether a particular request traversed it.
FP8 selects NativeMoEWrapper. utils/amx.py imports compiled AMXFP8_MOE/AVX2FP8_MOE and checks availability; native CPU expert kernels are real, but cover expert computation only.

Compiled extension declares AVX-512 FP8 decode/BF16 execution and block-E4M3-128x128 layout when the required ISA macros are built; separate AMXFP8 and AVX2FP8 bindings occur at962 and995. These are source dispatch facts, not a new binary acceptance.

Pinned expert prefill transport creates CUDA streams/events and submits host-to-device cudaMemcpyAsync. Disabling this optional staging would not remove the model attention or stream-wrapper requirements.

wrapper_gate.fact: GPU identity/free-memory/temperature admission and exact Docker GPU binding are protective deployment gates. Removing them cannot supply missing CPU serving implementations. Preserved unchanged.

required_scope: Implement/integrate a full CPU KDA prefill path and supported DSA/KPool backend/state lifecycle.
Replace CUDA stream expert integration and any required GPU allocations/transport with CPU execution scheduling.
Resolve checkpoint-native FP8 non-expert kernel support on target ISA; dequantization or alternate quantization would change the comparison.
Qualify complete model loading, semantic/tool parity, memory reserve, latency, occupied context and output limits before any production use.
